articles.headline: Intrigue surrounds possible reaction by Cleveland fans to Watson as Browns, Panthers look to go 2-1
articles.description: — The biggest question going into Sunday's game between the Carolina Panthers and Cleveland Browns may not be about the on-field matchups....
articles.body:
BEREA, Ohio -- — The biggest question going into Sunday's game between the Carolina Panthers and Cleveland Browns may not be about the on-field matchups. It's probably about the reception embattled quarterback Deshaun Watson will get from fans in Cleveland's first regular-season home game.


              Watson passed for 238 yards and two touchdowns in last Sunday's 23-19 win at Tampa Bay to temporarily silence calls for replacing him with Shedeur Sanders. That probably will not be enough to quiet the boos from the Dawg Pound and other sections of the stadium where some fans see the Browns' 2022 trade for Watson as one of the worst in NFL history.


              Browns coach Todd Monken said again this week that one way for Watson to get fans back on his side is to play well.


              “What does every fan want? Good football, a chance to win, be proud of their team. I mean, that’s what everybody wants. I’m excited to come back home and play, because I know the most important thing is seeing the Browns win,” Monken said.


              Watson, whose 76.9% completion rate is second in the NFL, said he didn't know if he would get more support after getting the Browns to 1-1. They haven't been 2-1 since 2023.


              “He balled (last week). People will say what they want about him, but when he puts that helmet on he comes ready to play. So we have to be ready. He can make every throw. He’s ready to lead those guys to a victory, so we have to show up," Panthers cornerback Mike Jackson said.


              The Browns are hoping to get their run game going after averaging only 65.5 yards over the first two games. The Panthers, meanwhile, allowed 291 yards on the ground in their Week 1 loss to Chicago but only 68 last week in their 34-3 victory at Atlanta.


              Carolina, looking to go 2-1 for the first time since 2021, comes into the game with one of the league's top passing attacks. Bryce Young is second in total touchdowns (seven) and passing yards (648). He also leads the league with nine completions of at least 25 yards.


              Young is also looking to become the fourth player with at least 275 passing yards, three touchdown passes and a passer rating of 100 or higher in each of the first three games.


              Cleveland hasn't allowed a 300-yard passer in its last 47 games.


              “I think it is just trusting each other and execution. (Past success) doesn’t entitle you to anything. It’s 0-0 when we start, so we have to flush it. We have a ton of respect for them and we have to be at our best against their defense," Young said.


              Need to know
              Carolina (1-1) at Cleveland (1-1)


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, FOX


              Latest odds: Panthers by 2 1/2


              Against the spread: Panthers 1-1; Browns 1-1.


              Last week: Panthers beat the Falcons 34-3; Browns beat the Buccaneers 23-19.


              La

articles.headline: NFL Week 3's best arrivals, led by Jordan Love
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.body:
Three weeks into the NFL season, players are continuing to set the tone before they ever step on the field.

Game-day arrivals have become their own weekly showcase, with statement pieces, designer looks and carefully chosen details turning stadium entrances into runways. And as the season settles in, the bar only gets higher.

Week 3 brings another chance to make an impression. Here are some of the best arrivals from around the NFL.

Thursday Night Fashion

The Green Bay Packers host the Atlanta Falcons to kick off Week 3's slate, and quarterback Jordan Love entered the home opener in style, pairing an oversize studded leather pullover with black trousers, a crisp white shirt and black tie. He completed the look with dark sunglasses and a checkered duffel bag.

articles.headline: The fallout from a blowout 2022 loss to the Rams ultimately ushered in a new era for the Broncos
articles.description: — All Courtland Sutton has to do is glance around at practice to fully grasp the level of changes since the last time the Denver Broncos played the...
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- — All Courtland Sutton has to do is glance around at practice to fully grasp the level of changes since the last time the Denver Broncos played the Los Angeles Rams.


              New coach. New quarterback. Brand new training facility. Newish ownership group. 


              Definitely new attitude.


              When Denver lost to a Baker Mayfield-led Rams team 51-14 on Christmas Day in 2022, it set in motion a chain of events that ultimately led to where the Broncos are today, with coach Sean Payton in charge and QB Bo Nix behind center. The Walton-Penner family ownership group, in charge for just a few months at the time of that loss, has been upgrading the franchise ever since. There's a cutting-edge training facility that opened this summer and a stadium concept that's in the planning stages.


              Sutton, one of those around that afternoon when the Rams dissected the Broncos so thoroughly that it led to the firing of coach Nathaniel Hackett the next day, marvels at how far the team has traveled. The Broncos (1-1) reached the AFC title game a season ago, while the Rams (1-1) played for the NFC title.


              “Everyone understands what the expectations are around here,” said Sutton, whose team tries to snap a five-game skid to the Rams on Sunday night. “It's nice to be in this realm where we are right now.” 


              These teams have coaches who share a common mentor — Jon Gruden. Payton worked with Gruden while both were in Philadelphia, and Rams coach Sean McVay was an assistant to Gruden in Tampa Bay.


              “I consider him a good friend,” Payton said of McVay. “He’s sharp. You watch his film, it’s good film always to watch. ... It’ll be a good challenge.”


              For Denver, a big challenge is stopping 38-year-old Matthew Stafford and an explosive Rams offensive. They may or may not have back receiver Puka Nacua from injury but still have Davante Adams, who had 195 yards and two TDs in a 28-6 win over the New York Giants on Monday night.


              “I’ve always watched him, looked up to him and admired the way he plays the game,” Nix said of Stafford. “He’s just always been fun to watch.”


              Adding to the challenge is finding a way to contain one of the best defensive linemen of all time in Aaron Donald, who returned to the field against the Giants for the first time since a playoff game in January 2024.


              Keep an eye on this: Adams going against Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II. Adams caught a winning TD in overtime against Surtain during the 2022 season, when the veteran receiver played for the Raiders.


              “That was a good memory for me,” Adams said. “I have a lot of respect for a lot of guys, but he’s definitely up there as far as one of the ones I have the most respect for.”


              Need to know
              Los Angeles Rams (1-1) at Denver (1-1).


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 8:20 p

articles.headline: Vikes' Murray says he recovered 'pretty quickly' from Week 1 concussion
articles.description: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray said he was over the symptoms from his Week 1 concussion "pretty quickly" and that being placed in protocol was "just part of the process."
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was "good pretty quickly" after suffering a scary concussion in Week 1, he said Thursday in his first public comments since the injury.

"Obviously with the protocol and everything like that, I had to go through it," Murray said of missing the Vikings' Week 2 game against the Chicago Bears. "It was just part of the process."

Murray was briefly motionless, with his body in a fencing posture, following what he acknowledged was an "awkward" slide at the end of a scramble on his 11th snap of the game. Two members of the Green Bay Packers' defense, defensive end Lukas Van Ness and safety Javon Bullard, converged on him as he hit the ground. Bullard was penalized for unnecessary roughness, but neither player was fined.

Murray said the only other concussion of his career, in a 2015 game when he was a freshman at Texas A&M, also occurred at the end of a slide.

"But I've really never had an issue protecting myself," he said. "I'd like to think I'm one of the least-hit quarterbacks in the league as far as just protecting myself, getting the ball out, stuff like that. So that's new for me to have to go through that type of situation, because that's the last thing I ever expected is to get a concussion just because I am very careful with being in open field and I know that was kind of an awkward slide situation, but I'm always trying to protect myself."

Murray had thrown an interception on his first pass and finished 3-of-5 for 18 yards. He also scrambled twice for 9 yards.

"Honestly, I just felt like I didn't even get to get in the game," he said. "That's what it felt like. It started and it was over."

The Vikings are 2-0 behind backup Carson Wentz, but they always intended to get Murray back in the lineup whenever he was ready.

Sunday, he'll face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and quarterback Baker Mayfield, his former teammate at Oklahoma. Murray referred to Mayfield as "my guy" and responded jokingly to Mayfield's remark this week that he "understands" why some people don't like Murray.

"I got to see him every day in college, so I respect the hell out of Baker and what he's been through and what type of player he is and person he is," Murray said. "They showed me the comment that he said about a lot of people don't like me or whatever. I say the same s--- about him.

"I think we're both competitors and we're going to do anything to win. So sometimes I might rub people the wrong way, but he's a great dude and a fierce competitor."

articles.headline: Goose at Dodger Stadium during Padres-Dodgers recalls past wildlife interruptions
articles.description: A goose slid on Dodger Stadium's field during Padres-Dodgers. It's not the first time a creature stole the show at a sporting event.
articles.body:
Sports are great. Animals are great. When the two mix, it's incredible -- sometimes. 

Fans at Dodger Stadium witnessed an unlikely instance of such a mix Wednesday, when a goose flew onto the field and slid stomach first in memorable fashion. 

This wasn't close to the first time an animal has become part of the game during a sporting event. There was the time a sportswriter's dog ran onto the field, interrupting a Georgia football game. And San Antonio seemingly has had as many bat encounters as "Dracula."

In honor of these amazing incidents, let's look back at some other top animal-on-field moments. 

What: Goose

Where: Chicago

When: 2026

A goose patrolled the field in the bottom of the third inning during the Cubs' game against the Phillies in April. Play continued and Cubs first baseman Michael Busch recorded a hit. The baseball flew over the goose, prompting the animal to fly away.

What: Dog

Where: Tesero, Italy

When: 2026

During the Winter Olympics, a local Czechoslovakian wolfdog named Nazgul managed to get away from his owner's sight and dash onto the homestretch of the cross-country ski course in Lago di Tesero -- during the race. Luckily, there was no serious disruption to the race, a preliminary qualifying round, spare for a few seconds of confusion shaved off the times of active racers who witnessed Nazgul's trot.

"I was like, 'Am I hallucinating?'" said Tena Hadzic, a 21-year-old Croatian skier who was among the participants whose time on the homestretch portion of the race coincided with the dog. "I don't know what I should do, because maybe he could attack me, bite me."

Nazgul was quickly corralled and returned home, but not before he endeared himself to spectators and viewers back home.

What: Squirrel

Where: New York, New York

When: 2025

A squirrel emerged in the fourth inning of a Yankees-Red Sox rivalry game from behind home plate, stopping right at Jhostynxon Garcia's left foot. The rodent took off again and stopped at the third-base foul line before attempting to dig a hole in front of the mound and then scampering down the right-field line to search for a way out.

What: Squirrel 

Where: Detroit, Michigan

When: 2025

The squirrel scampered around the outfield, eventually making its way to the warning track before climbing into the Tigers' bullpen during the first inning of the San Francisco Giants-Detroit Tigers match.

What: Snake

Where: Charlotte, North Carolina

When: 2025

Golfers and patrons had a front-row experience with the entanglement of sports and animals during the second round of the 2025 PGA Championship when a snake disrupted the contest.

The snake slithered its way through the course -- with the ball seemingly being its target before moving past it.

What: Bunny

Where: Norman, Oklahoma

When: 2025

During a college baseball matchup at L. Dale Mitchell Park, a bunny disrupted the contest.

With two outs in the top of the fourth inning, a bunny appeared on the third-base side. The animal star

articles.headline: Bills coach Brady unsatisfied with 2-0 start as Buffalo prepares to host winless Chargers
articles.description: — To hear Joe Brady express his concerns, it would be easy to think the Buffalo Bills opened the season winless instead of 2-0.
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- — To hear Joe Brady express his concerns, it would be easy to think the Buffalo Bills opened the season winless instead of 2-0.


              Perhaps it was the rookie coach’s way of getting his message across to not overlook Buffalo’s next opponent — the Los Angeles Chargers, who are winless as they hit the road for Sunday's game.


              “The house isn’t catching on fire, but smoke is showing,” said Brady, who even questioned a Josh Allen-led offense that has finished 10 of 18 possessions — not ending in kneeldowns — with touchdowns.


              “With the crew that we have, I’m (unhappy) every time we don’t (score a TD), if I’m being honest, and that’s not cocky,” Brady said.


              The Bills have hardly been perfect and their new-look defense has issues to sort after allowing 31 points and 24-plus first downs in each of its first two outings.


              But that’s nothing compared to the Chargers. LA has opened the season with two losses for the first time since 2017, committed more turnovers (five) than scored TDs (four), has injury concerns and lost both games by the same — 26-14 — to Arizona and Las Vegas.


              Despite opening with two home games, the Chargers have yet to hold a lead. They had a punt blocked and also surrendered a safety on tackle Joe Alt's holding penalty in the end zone last week. And Justin Herbert has already been sacked six times.


              “I trust those guys in the locker room, so I don’t think anyone has panicked or is worried because that’s not going to do us any good,” Herbert said. “It’s moving on to the next play and understanding we’re close. We’ve made mistakes, and how do we fix them?”


              The Bills followed a 36-31 season-opening win at Houston with a 41-31 win against Detroit four days later. And Buffalo has had the benefit of an expanded break to rest and analyze its deficiencies.


              The time was certainly welcome on defense, with Buffalo introducing four new starters and a 3-4 system.


              “I think I think all of us on defense left (the field) angry,” linebacker Terrel Bernard said, referring to the win over Detroit. “We’ve had time to kind of go back and understand where we’ve made mistakes and where we need to get better. Now it’s time to go do it.”


              Need to know
              Los Angeles Chargers (0-2) at Buffalo (2-0)


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, Fox.


              Latest odds: Bills by 7 1/2.


              Against the spread: Chargers 0-2; Bills 2-0.


              Last week: Chargers lost to the Raiders 26-14; Bills beat the Lions 41-31.


              Last meeting: Bills beat the Chargers 24-22 on Dec. 23, 2023, in LA.


              Series record: Chargers lead 25-14-2.


              Matchup to watch
              Bills pass rush vs. Chargers O-line. The Bills don’t blitz much, but have combined for seven sacks in two games,

articles.headline: Bob Pettit, who starred at LSU and then in NBA, dies at 93
articles.description: Bob Pettit, who was named an All-Star in each of his 11 NBA seasons and was one of the greatest scorers and rebounders in league history, died, the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame said Thursday.
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- Bob Pettit, an imposing scorer and rebounder for the St. Louis Hawks and winner of the NBA's first MVP award in 1956, has died. He was 93.

Pettit's alma mater, LSU, announced Thursday that he died a day earlier. The university did not provide a cause of death.

Pettit was an All-American at LSU before going on to the NBA, where he was an All-Star for each of his 11 seasons, all with the Hawks. He led them to the 1958 championship over the mighty Boston Celtics, the Hawks' lone title.

He was also the NBA MVP in 1959 and was the MVP of the All-Star Game four times, an achievement matched only by Los Angeles Lakers great Kobe Bryant.

Pettit was a force at a time when the NBA featured the likes of Wilt Chamberlain, Bill Russell, Oscar Robertson and Elgin Baylor. But it was also before the NBA was widely seen on television, and Pettit -- playing in a smaller market -- was denied a larger audience.

At 6-foot-9 and 205 pounds, Pettit was a physical presence at power forward before such a position became part of basketball's vocabulary. He rarely missed a game. He also played center and was one of the first big men who did not play solely with his back to the basket.

Pettit was the Rookie of the Year in 1954-55, the last season the Hawks played in Milwaukee before moving to St. Louis.

He captured the MVP the next season, leading the league in scoring at 25.7 points a game. He also was the NBA's scoring leader in 1959 at 29.2 points.

He retired after the 1964-65 season with career averages of 26.4 points and 16.2 rebounds. At that time, he was the NBA's career leader in points (20,880) and second in rebounds (12,849).

He was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1970.

"Lean, graceful, and always well-conditioned, Bob Pettit's physical build made him one of the first big men to play facing the basket," reads Pettit's biographical profile at the Hall of Fame. "But Pettit's resolve set him apart from his peers; he simply would not be outworked."

On social media Thursday, the Hall of Fame called Pettit a "sleek, skilled big man who revolutionized the forward position," adding that he was a "true giant of the game." 

Robert Lee Pettit Jr. was born on Dec. 12, 1932, in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. His father worked in law enforcement and served as East Baton Rouge Parish sheriff. Pettit was a late bloomer in basketball, not making the Baton Rouge High School varsity until his junior season.

As a senior, he led Baton Rouge to a state championship and wound up with more than a dozen college offers. He chose to stay home and starred at LSU as a sophomore, an era when players could not join the varsity until then.

He led the SEC in scoring all three of his seasons, with averages of 25.5 points as a sophomore, 24.9 as a junior and 31.4 as a senior.

Pettit is one of only three LSU players -- Pete Maravich and Shaquille O'Neal the others -- to earn a place in the Hall of Fame. Bronze statues of Pettit and O'Neal stand o

articles.headline: Anthony Gordon: Premier League players most fatigued at summer tournaments
articles.description: Anthony Gordon has said Premier League players are destined to come into summer tournaments more fatigued than any other league.
articles.body:
Anthony Gordon has said Premier League players are destined to come into summer tournaments more fatigued than any other league.

The inquest into England's painful World Cup semifinal defeat to Argentina continues, with focus on their energy-sapping style of football and inability to keep the ball in the same way that Spain can.

Boss Tuchel said fatigue played a part in their capitulation, coming on the back of extra time in their quarterfinal win against Norway in Miami heat and emotionally-draining victories against Congo DR and Mexico.

Gordon says those playing in the relentlessness of the Premier League are at a disadvantage at the back end of tournaments.

"I think that would probably be a fact," he said. "I don't know the stats, but I think for sure because in England, I'm not saying there is an easy game in any other leagues, but every game is as hard as the next.

"Playing Arsenal is the same as playing a newly-promoted side. That's the difficulty of the Premier League. Every game is so intense. Anyone can win a game.

"I mean, I think Hull, a newly-promoted team, were unbeaten until they played Newcastle.

"So that shows the strength of the Premier League, the strength of the English game, and I think for the English players playing in the Premier League, it would be a lot tougher on the body than players elsewhere."

Gordon's substitution in the semifinal remains a big talking point -- he was withdrawn 16 minutes after putting his side 1-0 up and replaced by a defender.

- Tuchel's England dilemma: Emulate Spain or embrace Premier League 'chaos'?

- Bukayo Saka: 'Tough' to stay on England bench in Argentina World Cup loss

- Harry Kane: Argentina defeat was most painful England moment yet

The game quickly unravelled after that and Gordon said that match needed a lot of unpacking in his personal diary afterwards.

"It was more than one page, I can tell you that," he added. "Maybe not consistently, but I always like to write things down. It just makes you feel more clear.

"I think everyone does that in a different way. Some people use laptops, or some people don't like to do anything.

"My version of that has always been just to write it down, and I kind of like it because I can look back on it and pass it on to my kids.

"But the Argentina game was probably the most memorable one I've had because I didn't really know what to write. I wrote down just pure emotion of what I felt.

"Obviously, I won't go into those details, but it was it was a good few pages, I can tell you."
